new_statements.rule_in_words: Kpan (Kente dialect) is a three-level-tone language; LAPSyD, coding from Shimizu 1971 chapter 1, records no word stress ('Assumed none'), i.e. the primary source is taken to be silent on stress rather than to state its position.
new_statements.exceptions: None; LAPSyD notes some unanalyzed HL and ML falling tones.
new_statements.domain_note: Database-level statement about the lexical phonology of the Kente dialect as described by Shimizu 1971; no word/phrase distinction discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All Kpan phonological data in circulation (LAPSyD 445, UPSID/PHOIBLE 424, WALS kpa) trace to Shimizu 1971 on the Kente (Kenti) dialect, spoken near Takum; Kpan has several other dialects (Kpwate/Hwaso, Ikpan/Kpanten, Eregba, Abakan, Nyonyo, Ibukwo per Glottolog alternative names), all under kpan1246. Do not confuse with Welmers 1968 'Jukun of Takum' = Jukun Takum [jbu] / Wapan, a different Jukunoid language.
